entries.name: Aegis
entries.description: The Bulwark's big sibling - a shield that walks, built by someone who believed the best weapon is the enemy's wasted time.
entries.tactics: Fourteen HP of pure blockade with painful contact damage. Aegis walls come escorted - Wardens hide behind them lobbing homing bolts. Breaking the shield head-on costs seconds you may not have; going around costs position. Decide fast, commit fully.

entries.name: Bulwark
entries.description: A slab of walking iron with no gun, no eyes, and no doubts. The host does not expect Bulwarks to win battles - only to make you late for them.
entries.tactics: High HP, slow descent, no attack; pure blockade. Behind one there is usually something shooting - a Warden's homing bolts curve around it. Either commit to breaking the wall fast or hold your fire and slip around; half-measures waste your damage into iron while the escort works.

entries.name: Chanter
entries.description: It rings a warning before its circle of bells tolls - not out of fairness, but ceremony. The host insists on its rituals.
entries.tactics: Telegraphs (pulses violet-white) before releasing an eight-bullet ring. The pulse is your timer: be moving AWAY when it fires, and the ring's gaps carry you through. Killing it mid-telegraph cancels the toll entirely.

entries.name: Colossus
entries.description: A fortress given legs and a grudge. Nothing gets through a Colossus until everything does - the host builds them to define where the battle happens.
entries.tactics: Massive HP (miniboss bar), heavy contact, slow walk, no gun. It is terrain that moves. Do not duel it while anything else shoots - use its own shadow as cover from enemies above it, and grind it down when the screen allows.

entries.name: Darter
entries.description: Fast, fragile, and utterly without fear. Darters are the host's messengers, and the message is always the same: you have less time than you think.
entries.tactics: Very fast, no gun - its body is the weapon. It crosses the screen in a couple of seconds, so treat every Darter lane as briefly poisoned. One hit kills it; snap shots work, but simply not being in its column is cheaper.

entries.name: Descender
entries.description: The rank and file of the endless host. Nobody remembers mustering them; they were simply always falling, rank after rank, like violet rain that learned to hold a spear. Alone, one is nothing. The host has never sent one alone.
entries.tactics: Falls straight down at a steady pace and fires a single green bolt straight ahead on a fixed cooldown. It never aims, so standing anywhere but directly beneath it is safe. Two hits end it - clear them early before bigger threats arrive, and never let a row of them fence you in.

entries.name: DreadCaptain
entries.description: The host's field officer, all black iron and gold plume. Captains do not fall with their soldiers. They arrive where the fighting is worst, on purpose.
entries.tactics: A 40-HP MINIBOSS (tracked bar) firing telegraphed aimed triple-volleys in bursts of three. The volleys converge on your position - strafe THROUGH them, not away. Its slow march gives you time; its escort usually does not. Priority: escorts first, then the long grind.

entries.name: Grudge
entries.description: A scrap of the dark with one violet eye, drifting among the crowds you actually want to shoot. It wants to be killed. That is the trap.
entries.tactics: CURSED: killing it JAMS your gun for four seconds - it pulses a dark aura as warning. It has no weapon; its whole job is to swim between real targets and eat your stray bullets. Check your line of fire before you hold the trigger. Sometimes the strongest shot is the one you do not take.

entries.name: Harbinger
entries.description: A turning wheel of violet omens. What it announces has never once been good news.
entries.tactics: Fires a rotating six-bolt ring (violet, telegraphed) - each volley steps a few degrees, so the safe angle NEVER stays. Keep circling in one direction and the gaps come to you; freeze and the wheel finds you. Kill it during the telegraph pauses.

entries.name: Hexblade
entries.description: Twin blades that fell from the same forge and never separated. They snake as they fall, and the wall they draw between you and the sky bends like a living thing.
entries.tactics: Fires paired green walls that snake (sine motion - violet bullets). The wall's gap oscillates: watch one full period before committing to a lane. The Hexblade itself weaves fast; it dies in three hits if you can pin it.

entries.name: Hexer
entries.description: A quiet curse-monger. Hexers rarely kill anyone themselves; they make the sky complicated, and the complicated sky kills you.
entries.tactics: Fires slow crossing bolts on fixed diagonals. One Hexer is trivial; three turn the screen into a braid. Their shots are the slowest on screen - track them peripherally and prioritize the enemies forcing you to move.

entries.name: Hunter
entries.description: The host's bloodhound. It does not patrol, it does not guard - it points its whole falling body at where you are and corrects.
entries.tactics: Tracks your horizontal position while descending - it will be above you. Its dive is the threat; sidestep late and it cannot correct in time. Killing it early spares you the pressure entirely.

entries.name: Inquisitor
entries.description: A tall crimson hood with a white slit where questions come out. Its brands do not ask where you are. They ask where you will be.
entries.tactics: Telegraphs, then fires TWIN red homing brands in quick succession. The first pulls your dodge; the second punishes it. Break line by moving hard perpendicular through both, or kill it during the telegraph. High value target - never let two Inquisitors sync.

entries.name: Lancer
entries.description: A splinter of steel with a single idea. The bolt it fires leaves the barrel almost lazily, as if stretching - then remembers its purpose all at once.
entries.tactics: Fires a green bolt that starts slow and accelerates hard. Your instinct calibrates on the launch speed and is wrong by the time it reaches you - dodge EARLY, when the bolt is born, not when it looks close. The Lancer itself dives fast; two hits kill it.

entries.name: Marauder
entries.description: Pressure incarnate. Marauders do not duel; they lean on you, volley after paired volley, until something - usually you - gives.
entries.tactics: Fires green arcs in quick two-bursts. The second burst comes fast after the first - never dodge into the space the first volley herded you toward. Mid HP; focus fire between bursts.

entries.name: Orbiter
entries.description: A violet ring that pins airspace the way a nail pins a map. The cross it fires is not aimed at you; it is aimed at everywhere you might want to go.
entries.tactics: Fires four bolts in a fixed diagonal cross, claiming lanes rather than chasing you. The gaps between the cross arms are always safe - learn the X shape and sit in its blind wedges while you burn it down.

entries.name: Pyromancer
entries.description: Its fan of fire starts lazy, almost decorative - and then pounces like a cat that was only pretending to sleep.
entries.tactics: Fires an aimed three-bolt fan that ACCELERATES. The safe gap you see at launch closes fast - pick your dodge lane immediately and commit. Kill it high; an accelerating fan from low altitude is nearly unreactable.

entries.name: Ravager
entries.description: Slow, heavy, patient. A Ravager has never hurried in its existence, because its bolt does the hurrying - for a little while.
entries.tactics: Fires a red HOMING bolt that hunts you for about a second before flying straight. Red means hunted: move perpendicular and keep moving until it gives up the chase, then let it pass. High HP and heavy contact - respect its body too.

entries.name: Reliquary
entries.description: A dark shrine with a violet gem where a heart should be. Whatever is sealed inside was sealed for a reason - and your bullets are a key.
entries.tactics: CURSED miniboss: a 30-HP walking shrine whose death makes you LEADEN (slow) for four seconds. It blocks like an Aegis, so the temptation to break it is constant - but time your kill for a calm moment, or dodge around it and leave the seal alone. The aura pulse marks the price.

entries.name: Sentinel
entries.description: A patient eye in a bronze shell. Sentinels were the first of the host to look down and see YOU rather than a battlefield - and they have not looked away since.
entries.tactics: Descends slowly and fires single green bolts aimed at your position when it shoots. The bolt flies straight after launch: sidestep AFTER it fires, not before, or you dodge into the next one. Low HP - a priority target while it is still high on the screen.

entries.name: Seraph
entries.description: A white-violet wheel that sings when it turns. The host does not know where the Seraphs came from either. They arrived; the host made room.
entries.tactics: Weaves while releasing a rotating TEN-bolt wheel (telegraphed, violet). Dense but slow - hug the rim of one gap and rotate with it. The weave makes its position drift, so re-anchor after every volley. Twelve HP; commit real fire to it.

entries.name: Skirmisher
entries.description: A kite of red-brown leather that refuses to hold still. Skirmishers weave because a moving sniper is a living sniper - and they aim because living is not enough.
entries.tactics: Weaves while firing aimed green bolts. The weave makes it annoying to hit - lead its sine, or wait for the turnaround points where it briefly hangs. Its shots come at YOUR position: keep moving and they land behind you.

entries.name: Spinner
entries.description: It fell spinning once, by accident, and the host decided the terror was worth keeping. The spiral it trails has a hypnotist's patience.
entries.tactics: Sheds a slow rotating spiral of shots as it descends. Individual bullets are slow; the danger is the lattice they leave across lanes you wanted later. Cut it down early or accept fighting inside its web.

entries.name: Warden
entries.description: A teal lantern that guards the walls. Wardens learned the oldest lesson of siegecraft: the archer behind the wall outlives the archer on it.
entries.tactics: The escort gun: slow, always behind a Bulwark or Aegis in the same lane, firing red homing bolts that curve around its shield. You cannot hit it until the wall dies - so either break the wall fast or dodge the bolts and starve it of a target. Red bullets hunt; keep moving perpendicular.

entries.name: Warlock
entries.description: It carries a ring of violet fire the way a monk carries a prayer - constantly, and for someone else's benefit. The detonation is the sermon.
entries.tactics: Descends and periodically releases a full ring of bullets in every direction. The ring is dense near the Warlock and sparse far away - distance is armor. Kill it between rings, and never fight it point-blank.

entries.name: Weaver
entries.description: A Descender that learned doubt. It swings across the sky as it falls, never quite committing to a lane, scattering short arcs of shot as if sowing a field.
entries.tactics: Weaves side to side while dropping and lobs a small green arc downward. Its position is predictable - a smooth sine - so lead it slightly when you shoot. The arc punishes you for standing still; keep drifting and it never touches you.

entries.name: Wisp
entries.description: A pale mote that would be beautiful if it were not so numerous. One Wisp is a firefly. Forty are a funeral.
entries.tactics: Tiny, fast, weaving, no gun - kills by touch. Swarms fill lanes faster than you can clear them; sweep them with your fire's natural spread while dealing with real shooters. Never chase one into a crowd.

entries.name: Zealot
entries.description: A blade of white gold that dives like judgement. Zealots believe - in what, nobody has survived long enough to ask.
entries.tactics: Very fast diver with an aimed bolt that accelerates viciously. Two threats in one: the bolt commits you to a dodge, and the diving body punishes the dodge. Kill it at the top of the screen or give its lane away entirely.

entries.name: Archon
entries.description: A star of judgement that never learned mercy's spelling. Its wrath calls zealots; its ascension calls wardens; its light calls walls.
entries.tactics: Wide fans and rotating crosses, then sweeping walls plus Zealot summons (Wrath), then rings, homing bolts, and Warden summons (Ascension). The summons are the real pressure - clear Zealots before their dives sync with the walls. White tint means final phase: maximum speed, keep to the bottom corners.

entries.name: Behemoth
entries.description: A wall of iron that learned to fight back. Everything the Behemoth throws is heavy, including the silence between volleys.
entries.tactics: Accelerating fans, massive slow walls, offset and dense rings across three phases. Its bullets are heavy but sparse - the fight is about patience, not reflexes. Punish the long recovery after each wall; by Meltdown (red glow) the floor is mostly bullets, so pre-plan lanes.

entries.name: Eternity
entries.description: A white void ring that was here before the host and intends to be here after. Stillness. Motion. Eternity. It has only ever needed three words.
entries.tactics: Stillness lays cross-quads through sine curtains - deceptively calm; learn its spacing. Motion (65%) adds a spiral and Hexblade summons. Eternity (35%) is dense rings, storm crosses, and the gyre at 1.6x hover with Ravagers hunting you. The hardest fight in the game; every powerup cap and every color rule you have learned is the entry fee.

entries.name: The Gatekeeper
entries.description: The first bell of the Run. The Gatekeeper does not hate you; it simply was built into the doorway, and you are knocking. Every knight meets it. Most meet it again.
entries.tactics: The tutorial boss: aimed shots, a modest fan, a phase flip at half HP. Its openers are slow and generously spaced - use the fight to practice reading telegraphs and phase tints. If the Gatekeeper is costing you hearts, later gates will cost the run.

entries.name: Herald
entries.description: It announces the wall, then becomes it. The Herald believes a proclamation should be legible from anywhere on the battlefield - so it writes in bullets, edge to edge.
entries.tactics: Sweeping telegraphed walls with deliberate gaps, plus aimed jabs to herd you. Find the gap EARLY - the wall crosses slowly but totally. Below half HP (Judgement, white tint) a rotating cross joins; track the cross's turn and treat the walls as the metronome.

entries.name: Lich
entries.description: Green curtains of grave-light, swaying as they fall. The Lich conducts them like a choir, and below half health the phalanx begins to march.
entries.tactics: Sine curtains (violet snaking walls) with fast aimed spit underneath. The curtains breathe - their gaps slide in waves; move WITH the wave, not against it. Requiem (below half) adds a snaking phalanx wall: keep to the screen's lower third and thread the oscillation.

entries.name: Monarch
entries.description: The old king of the endless host. Three reigns, each crueller than the last, and a court of bullets that never stops bowing.
entries.tactics: Three phases stacking cross-quads, dense rings, and spirals. Phase entries are pulsed and tinted - the moment it flashes, reposition to open space before the new pattern's first volley. The dense ring's gaps are narrow but honest; the spiral rewards circling with it.

entries.name: Oblivion
entries.description: The last thing most far runs see. A near-black orb with a violet rim, dense rings, a turning spiral, and the dark that follows you home.
entries.tactics: Dense rings with aimed spit, then a spiral (Maw, plus Hexblade summons), then cross-quads with homing bolts and a Ravager (Oblivion phase). The rings are the rhythm section - everything else syncopates around them. Below 30% the hover doubles; stop aiming at where it is.

entries.name: Serpent
entries.description: Two fangs, one appetite. The Serpent crosses its own fire because it long ago stopped distinguishing between the battlefield and its jaws.
entries.tactics: Aimed spit from alternating fangs plus crossing diagonal volleys that lattice the screen. The lattice tightens as it bleeds - the fight gets harder as you win, so bank your dodging stamina. Stay off the centerline where the crosses overlap.

entries.name: Stormcaller
entries.description: The storm follows you. Crosses of violet lightning turn about the Stormcaller as it hunts, and the thunder always aims.
entries.tactics: Capped red homing bolts plus rotating StormCross volleys. The homing bolts give up after a second - bait them wide, then cut back. Tempest (below 55%) adds a radial ring and speed: the crosses keep rotating, so never park in a gap; ride it.

entries.name: Summoner
entries.description: It does not fight you. It invites others to - and rings its bell while you drown in guests. The glowing core is the invitation list.
entries.tactics: Fights entirely through adds: Wisps in Ritual, Skirmishers in Legion (below 55%), with aimed spit and a telegraphed ring for punctuation. Kill the summons FIRST or they multiply past control - but watch your fire discipline near its ring telegraph. Its own HP melts fast once the court is empty.

entries.name: Tyrant
entries.description: It wears its ring of fire like a crown, and its triple volleys are decrees. The Tyrant does not tolerate standing still. It barely tolerates moving.
entries.tactics: Aimed triple volleys plus a wide fan, with an offset ring in its late phase. The triples come at your position - constant strafing beats reaction dodging. When the ring appears, the safe wedges rotate; find one and migrate with it.

entries.name: Warbringer
entries.description: A crimson war-totem with a gold eye that has already counted your hearts. The Warbringer does not summon soldiers. It PROMOTES them.
entries.tactics: Muster opens with wide fans and lance walls while a DREAD CAPTAIN miniboss marches in - kill the Captain before Onslaught (60%) triples the Zealot pressure. Warpath (30%) is rings plus homing under maximum speed. This is the wall the 40k crowd hits: bring maxed powerups or bring patience.
